Ten years ago, Midsummer-Milano was born

Dear friend,

ten years ago, Midsummer-Milano was born.

The name comes from the brightest day of the year — the summer solstice. At the time it was an idea: to bring Italian design into a world dominated by Northern European brands; to build beds the way fine furniture is built; to work only with natural fibres and with fabrics that deserved the same care as the product they were dressing.

What has changed in ten years.

We started with two artisans, they are still the same two. They build every Midsummer system from start to finish, over two or three days. We have not industrialised anything.

We started with horsehair, wool, and cashmere. Today we also work with vicuña, yak, and Orange Fiber. Each material is chosen for what it does, not for what it tells.

We started by dressing our beds in fabrics chosen one at a time. Today we dress Midsummer in Loro Piana Interiors — an arrangement we believe is unique in the world of luxury beds.

We started selling in Milan. Today our beds are in Italy, Russia, Greece, Poland, Canada, and within a few months, in the United States.

What has not changed.

The conviction that sleep is not a problem to be solved but a moment to be honoured. That real luxury is not a price but a decision not to compromise when it would be convenient to do so. That a bed should last at least twenty years, and that if it does not, it was not a bed.

Thank you.

To those who bought a Midsummer in these ten years. To those who visited the showroom out of curiosity. To those who have written about us. To those who follow these newsletters. To those who have introduced us to a friend. To those who, reading these lines, are thinking about the bed they are sleeping on tonight.

Ten years is many, and few, at the same time. What seems right to say today is that we are starting now.

Warm regards,
Chiara Mennini
Founder, Midsummer-Milano

Caro amico,

dieci anni fa nasceva Midsummer-Milano.

Il nome viene dal giorno più luminoso dell’anno — il solstizio d’estate. Cosa è cambiato in dieci anni.

Abbiamo cominciato con due artigiani, e sono ancora gli stessi due. Costruiscono ogni sistema Midsummer dall’inizio alla fine, in due o tre giorni. Non abbiamo industrializzato nulla.

Abbiamo cominciato con crine di cavallo, lana e cashmere. Oggi lavoriamo anche con vigogna, yak e Orange Fiber. Ogni materiale è scelto per ciò che fa, non per ciò che racconta.

Abbiamo cominciato vestendo i nostri letti con tessuti scelti uno alla volta. Oggi vestiamo Midsummer in Loro Piana Interiors — un accordo che crediamo unico nel mondo dei letti di lusso.

Abbiamo cominciato vendendo a Milano. Oggi i nostri letti sono in Italia, Russia, Grecia, Polonia, Canada e, tra pochi mesi, negli Stati Uniti.

Grazie.

A chi ha comprato un Midsummer in questi dieci anni. A chi è passato dallo showroom per curiosità. A chi ha scritto di noi. A chi segue queste newsletter. A chi ci ha presentato a un amico. A chi, leggendo queste righe, sta pensando al letto su cui dormirà stanotte.

Dieci anni sono tanti, e pochi, allo stesso tempo. Quello che oggi ci sembra giusto dire è che cominciamo adesso.

Дорогой друг,

десять лет назад родилась Midsummer-Milano.

Название пришло от самого светлого дня в году — летнего солнцестояния. Тогда это была идея: привнести итальянский дизайн в мир, где господствовали североевропейские марки; строить кровати так, как строят изысканную мебель; работать только с натуральными волокнами и с тканями, достойными той же заботы, что и изделие, которое они одевают.

Что изменилось за десять лет.

Мы начинали с двух мастеров — и это всё те же двое. Они создают каждую систему Midsummer от начала до конца, за два-три дня. Мы ничего не поставили на поток.

Мы начинали с конского волоса, шерсти и кашемира. Сегодня мы работаем также с викуньей, яком и Orange Fiber. Каждый материал выбран за то, что он делает, а не за то, что о нём рассказывают.

Мы начинали, одевая наши кровати в ткани, выбранные по одной. Сегодня мы одеваем Midsummer в Loro Piana Interiors — соглашение, которое, как мы считаем, уникально в мире роскошных кроватей.

Мы начинали с продаж в Милане. Сегодня наши кровати есть в Италии, России, Греции, Польше, Канаде, а через несколько месяцев — и в США.

Что не изменилось.

Убеждённость в том, что сон — не задача, которую нужно решить, а момент, который нужно чтить. Что настоящая роскошь — не цена, а решение не идти на компромисс, когда это было бы удобно. Что кровать должна служить не меньше двадцати лет, а если не служит — это была не кровать.

Спасибо.

Тем, кто купил Midsummer за эти десять лет. Тем, кто заглянул в шоурум из любопытства. Тем, кто писал о нас. Тем, кто читает эти рассылки. Тем, кто познакомил нас с другом. Тем, кто, читая эти строки, думает о кровати, на которой будет спать сегодня ночью.

Десять лет — это много и мало одновременно. Сегодня нам кажется правильным сказать, что мы только начинаем.

С теплом,
Chiara Mennini
основательница Midsummer-Milano

This is the first post in our occasional series on famous and noteworthy bedrooms.

 

Odysseus (Ulysses in latin) was the King of Ithaca, a very small and thoroughly barren island in the Ionian Sea. Odysseus was known throughout of Greece for his intelligence and his cunning. He was married to Penelope a strong and faithful woman, definitely a match for her more famous husband.

When the Trojans abducted Helena and the greek-trojan war began, Odysseus was recruited in the greek expedition against his will. But then he fought valiantly for ten years alongside the other greek kings and warriors to bring down the walls of Troy. Homer’s Iliad is of course the superb narration of those events. In it Homer credits Odysseus with conceiving the stratagem of the horse which would so bitterly deceit the trojans and eventually bring an end to the war and to the defeat and sack of Troy.

After the fall, those gods who had rooted for Troy were out to seek revenge (as you might expect) and found that Odysseus was the perfect target for their malignancy. They made it very very hard for him to get back home to Ithaca. Through many travails, a long voyage which took him across the best part of the eastern mediterranean and marvelous encounters, it took him a whole ten years to complete the journey. Homer’s Odyssey is the account of those long years.

When Odysseus finally arrives in Ithaca he has been gone for the best part of twenty years, ten years for the war and then another ten years to complete his journey back. Very uncertain of what he might find on the island and in his household he comes ashore in disguise and takes a look around. His kingdom is in disarray. 

His wife Penelope is still waiting for him and has not remarried, but a group of aggressive and voracious suitors are urging her to decide, while staying at the palace, feasting night and day and depleting the riches of the island. Odysseus at first is recognized by no one. Then by his old and dying dog, Argus. Then by the housekeeper when she is ritually washing his feet and recognizes an old scar on the former king’s leg. She is sworn to secrecy at the peril of her life.

When Penelope finally gives in to the suitors and declares that she will marry whoever can string Odysseus’s old rigid bow and shoot an arrow through the shaft of twelve axes, all her suitors try their luck in vain and finally give up.

Finally also the disguised Odysseus asks to have a try and is derided by all. But he has the strength to arm the bow and the skill to complete the shot. He wins the contest, reveals himself as the rightful king and promptly proceeds to kill all the suitors.

Penelope is now engaged to marry this man, but deep inside she is still uncertain of his identity. When together they enter the wedding chamber she orders her maid to move the bed. Odysseus immediately protests that this cannot be done.

The nuptial bed had been carved by him a long time ago from the gigantic trunk of an olive tree. The roots still run into the soil, the bed cannot be moved, the whole palace has been built around that unmovable bed.

Only Odysseus and Penelope know this very private secret of their bedroom. Penelope now recognizes her long-lost husband and the king and queen of Ithaca are finally reunited.

Thankfully Midsummer-Milano beds can be moved, but like Odysseus and Penelope’s wedding bed they are designed and built to form the center piece of your house.

Questo è il primo post della nostra serie occasionale sulle camere da letto famose e degne di nota.

Odisseo (Ulisse in latino) era il re di Itaca, un'isola molto piccola e completamente sterile nel Mar Ionio. Odisseo era noto in tutta la Grecia per la sua intelligenza e la sua astuzia. Era sposato con Penelope, una donna forte e fedele, sicuramente all'altezza del suo più famoso marito.

Quando i Troiani rapirono Elena e scoppiò la guerra greco-troiana, Odisseo fu reclutato nella spedizione greca contro la sua volontà. Ma poi combatté valorosamente per dieci anni al fianco degli altri re e guerrieri greci per abbattere le mura di Troia. L'Iliade di Omero è naturalmente la superba narrazione di quegli eventi. In essa Omero attribuisce a Odisseo l'ideazione dello stratagemma del cavallo che avrebbe ingannato così amaramente i Troiani e alla fine avrebbe posto fine alla guerra, alla sconfitta e al sacco di Troia.

Dopo la caduta, gli dei che avevano tifato per Troia erano in cerca di vendetta (come ci si poteva aspettare) e scoprirono che Odisseo era il bersaglio perfetto per la loro malvagità. Gli resero molto, molto difficile il ritorno a casa, a Itaca. Tra molte traversie, un lungo viaggio che lo portò ad attraversare gran parte del Mediterraneo orientale e incontri meravigliosi, gli ci vollero ben dieci anni per completare il viaggio. L'Odissea di Omero è il resoconto di quei lunghi anni.

Quando Odisseo finalmente arriva a Itaca, sono passati quasi vent'anni dalla sua partenza: dieci anni per la guerra e altri dieci per completare il viaggio di ritorno. Molto incerto su cosa potrebbe trovare sull'isola e nella sua casa, sbarca travestito e si guarda intorno. Il suo regno è in rovina.

Sua moglie Penelope lo sta ancora aspettando e non si è risposata, ma un gruppo di pretendenti aggressivi e voraci la sta spingendo a decidere, mentre soggiorna a palazzo, banchettando notte e giorno e prosciugando le ricchezze dell'isola. Odisseo all'inizio non viene riconosciuto da nessuno. Poi dal suo vecchio cane morente, Argo. Poi dalla governante quando, mentre gli lava ritualmente i piedi, riconosce una vecchia cicatrice sulla gamba dell'ex re. Giura di mantenere il segreto a rischio della sua vita.

Quando Penelope cede finalmente ai pretendenti e dichiara che sposerà chiunque riesca a tendere il vecchio arco rigido di Odisseo e a scoccare una freccia attraverso l'asta di dodici asce, tutti i pretendenti tentano la fortuna invano e alla fine rinunciano.

Infine anche Odisseo, travestito, chiede di provare e viene deriso da tutti. Ma ha la forza di armare l'arco e l'abilità di completare il tiro. Vince la gara, si rivela il legittimo re e procede prontamente a uccidere tutti i pretendenti.

Penelope è ora fidanzata con quest'uomo, ma nel profondo è ancora incerta sulla sua identità. Quando entrano insieme nella camera nuziale, ordina alla sua ancella di spostare il letto. Odisseo protesta immediatamente che ciò non è possibile.

Il letto nuziale era stato da lui ricavato molto tempo prima dal gigantesco tronco di un ulivo. Le radici affondano ancora nel terreno, il letto non può essere spostato, l'intero palazzo è stato costruito attorno a quel letto immobile.

Solo Odisseo e Penelope conoscono questo segreto privato della loro camera da letto. Penelope ora riconosce il marito perduto da tempo e il re e la regina di Itaca sono finalmente riuniti.

Fortunatamente i letti Midsummer-Milano possono essere spostati, ma come il letto nuziale di Ulisse e Penelope sono progettati e costruiti per costituire il fulcro della casa.

Это первый пост в нашей периодической серии статей о знаменитых и примечательных спальнях.

Одиссей (на латыни — Улисс) был царём Итаки, очень маленького и совершенно бесплодного острова в Ионическом море. Одиссей был известен по всей Греции своим умом и хитростью. Он был женат на Пенелопе, сильной и верной женщине, определённо достойной своего более знаменитого мужа.

Когда троянцы похитили Елену и началась греко-троянская война, Одиссей против своей воли был призван в греческий поход. Но затем он десять лет доблестно сражался бок о бок с другими греческими царями и воинами, чтобы разрушить стены Трои. «Илиада» Гомера, безусловно, является превосходным повествованием об этих событиях. В ней Гомер приписывает Одиссею изобретение хитрости с конём, которая так жестоко обманула троянцев и в конечном итоге привела к концу войны, поражению и разграблению Трои.

После падения Трои боги, болевшие за неё, вознамерились отомстить (как и следовало ожидать), и обнаружили, что Одиссей – идеальная мишень для их злобы. Они очень и очень осложнили ему возвращение домой, на Итаку. После многих терзаний, долгого путешествия, которое пролегало через лучшую часть восточного Средиземноморья, и удивительных встреч, ему потребовалось целых десять лет, чтобы завершить путешествие. «Одиссея» Гомера – это повествование об этих долгих годах.

Когда Одиссей наконец прибыл на Итаку, он отсутствовал почти двадцать лет: десять лет на войне и ещё десять лет на обратном пути. Не зная, что его ждёт на острове и в его доме, он переодетым сходит на берег и осматривается. Его царство в смятении.

Его жена Пенелопа всё ещё ждёт его и не вышла замуж повторно, но группа агрессивных и жадных женихов подталкивает её к решению, оставаясь во дворце, пируя день и ночь и опустошая богатства острова. Сначала Одиссея никто не узнаёт. Затем его узнаёт его старый умирающий пёс Аргус. Затем экономка, совершая ритуальное омовение его ног, замечает старый шрам на ноге бывшего царя. Она даёт ей клятву хранить тайну под страхом смерти.

Когда Пенелопа наконец уступает женихам и заявляет, что выйдет замуж за того, кто сможет натянуть старый жесткий лук Одиссея и пронзить стрелой древко двенадцати топоров, все ее женихи тщетно пытают счастье и в конце концов сдаются.

Брачное ложе было вырезано им давным-давно из гигантского ствола оливкового дерева. Корни всё ещё уходят в землю, ложе невозможно сдвинуть, весь дворец построен вокруг этого недвижимого ложа.

There are many reasons why we have called our company Midsummer.

Another reason is the obvious reference to Shakespeare's comedy. A Midsummer’s Night is set in a magical mythical forest and celebrates the dreamy sleep, the quiet and fairy night. A play that is full of unforgettable lines whose appeal resonates through the centuries.

Since we want to make our customers sleep well, like never before, we think that we have chosen a meaningful name.

“Are you sure/That we are awake? It seems to me/That yet we sleep, we dream” William Shakespeare

If you want to know what the plot of Shakespeare's play is like, here is a summary.

Theseus, duke of Athens, has conquered Hippolyta, the Amazon queen, and is about to wed her. Meanwhile, two lovers, Hermia and Lysander, seek refuge in the forest near Athens when Hermia’s father demands that she marry Demetrius. Hoping to win Demetrius’s favour, Helena tells him their whereabouts and follows him to the forest, where he goes in search of Hermia. The forest is also full of fairies who have come for the duke’s wedding. Oberon, the king of the fairies, quarrels with his queen, Titania, and bids his mischievous servant Puck to drop magic juice into her eyes as she sleeps; his intent is to punish her for her disobedience by causing her to fall hopelessly in love with whatever person or creature she happens to see when she awakes. Noting that the human lovers in the forest are also at odds, he orders Puck to drop the love juice into Demetrius’s eyes so that Demetrius’s one-time affection for Helena will be restored. Because the two young Athenian men look much alike, however, Puck mistakenly administers the love juice to Lysander, who then happens to see Helena when he awakes. He falls hopelessly in love with her. Now both young men are in love with Helena and neither with the poor deserted Hermia. This situation does not make Helena any happier, though. She comes to the conclusion that they are all making fun of her. Hermia and Helena fall out over this contretemps, while the young men have become fierce and even would-be murderous rivals of one another for Helena. All is at sixes and sevens.

In the same woods a group of artisans are rehearsing an entertainment for the duke’s wedding. Ever playful, Puck gives one of the “mechanicals,” Nick Bottom, an ass’s head; when Titania awakens, she falls in love with Bottom. After much general confusion and comic misunderstanding, Oberon’s magic restores Titania and the four lovers to their original states. The duke invites the two couples to join him and Hippolyta in a triple wedding. The wedding celebration features Bottom’s troupe in a comically inept performance of their play, The Most Lamentable Comedy and Most Cruel Death of Pyramus and Thisbe, which turns out to be a parody of the perilous encounters the various lovers have experienced in the forest and somehow managed to survive.

«Вы уверены, что мы бодрствуем? Мне кажется, что мы всё ещё спим и видим сны » Уильям Шекспир

Если вы хотите узнать сюжет пьесы Шекспира, вот его краткое содержание.

Тесей, герцог Афин , завоевал Ипполиту, царицу амазонок , и собирается жениться на ней. Тем временем двое влюбленных, Гермия и Лисандр, ищут убежища в лесу близ Афин, когда отец Гермии требует, чтобы она вышла замуж за Деметрия. Надеясь завоевать расположение Деметрия, Елена сообщает ему их местонахождение и следует за ним в лес, где он отправляется на поиски Гермии. Лес также полон фей, пришедших на свадьбу герцога. Оберон , король фей, ссорится со своей королевой Титанией и приказывает своему озорному слуге Паку капнуть ей в глаза волшебный сок, пока она спит; его намерение состоит в том, чтобы наказать ее за непослушание, заставив ее безнадежно влюбиться в любого человека или существо, которое она случайно увидит, когда проснется. Заметив, что человеческие влюблённые в лесу также в ссоре, он приказывает Паку капнуть любовный сок в глаза Деметрия, чтобы восстановить былую привязанность Деметрия к Елене. Dear Mindful Sleepers,

As we welcome the arrival of spring, there are many reasons to celebrate - the warmer weather, blooming flowers, and longer days are just a few. But did you know that spring can also have a positive impact on our sleep?

As the days get longer and the sun starts to shine, our bodies begin to produce more melatonin, the hormone that regulates sleep. This natural increase in melatonin can help us feel more tired at night, making it easier to fall and stay asleep.

In addition to the increase in melatonin, the warmer weather can also have a positive impact on our sleep. When our bodies are exposed to sunlight, we produce more vitamin D, which is important for regulating our circadian rhythms. This helps to improve our sleep-wake cycle and can lead to better quality sleep.

But it's not just the physical changes that make spring a great time for sleep - it's also the mental and emotional benefits. With the arrival of spring comes a sense of renewal and rejuvenation, which can help us to feel more relaxed and at ease. The beauty of the blooming flowers and fresh greenery can also have a calming effect on the mind, helping us to unwind and let go of any stress or tension.

So as we embrace the new season, let's also take the opportunity to prioritize our sleep. Make sure you're getting enough rest each night, and try to create a peaceful sleep environment that promotes relaxation and calm. And when you step outside and feel the warmth of the sun on your skin, take a moment to appreciate the beauty of the season and the positive impact it can have on your sleep.

Happy Spring, and sweet dreams!

Warmly,

The Midsummer team

Comfort and Support:

Natural fibers such as alpaca and cashmere offer unparalleled softness and comfort. Their natural elasticity allows them to conform to your body, providing personalized support that reduces pressure points. This can help prevent aches and pains, particularly in the back and joints.

MIDSUMMER MILANO — AUGUST LETTER
In praise of time, taste, and terroir.

Dear friend,

August in Italy is a ritual: shutters drawn at noon, sandals dusty with sun, and a chilled glass raised at dusk.

Italians have always believed in the pleasure of taking time — and nowhere is that more evident than in our wine. Much like a beautifully crafted bed, a fine Italian wine is a product of place, patience, and tradition.

At Midsummer, we think about wine the way we think about rest: with care for origin, respect for nature, and an eye for balance.

Wines that rest, like we do

Barolo (Piedmont)


Known as “the king of wines,” Barolo ages for years to reach its full depth. Made from Nebbiolo grapes, it’s structured, bold, and surprisingly elegant — a classic of Italian winemaking.

Brunello di Montalcino (Tuscany)


Earthy, full-bodied, and expressive, Brunello is made with 100% Sangiovese grapes and reflects the slow rhythms of Tuscany. Like our beds, it gets better with time.

Etna Rosso (Sicily)


From volcanic soil comes a vibrant, mineral-rich red. Etna Rosso is a testament to nature’s unpredictability — and the beauty that comes from it.

Fiano di Avellino (Campania)


Fresh and floral with hints of hazelnut, this white wine is sophisticated yet understated. It’s summer in a bottle, and a quiet luxury.

Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi (Marche)


A white with character — crisp, almondy, and complex. It pairs well with seafood and sea views.

Soave Classico (Veneto)


Light, dry, and mineral, Soave is one of Italy’s most refined whites — proof that simplicity can be a form of elegance.


What wine and rest share

Both ask us to pause. To appreciate process. To recognize that what is slow is not lost — but often more lasting, more beautiful, more true.

Whether it’s aged in barrels or sewn by hand, crafted with grapes or with wool — the best things are those made with intention.

This summer, we raise a glass to the culture of time. And to the Italian way of living — fully, softly, and with style.

Alla salute,
The Midsummer Milano Team
Natural luxury, made in Italy.

A great mattress does more than support the body; it quietly adapts to the seasons so your sleep remains deep and restorative all year. At Midsummer Milano, we design every bed with a dual personality. The summer side feels naturally cool and crisp; the winter side wraps the body in gentle warmth. Together they create a breathable, balanced microclimate that keeps temperature and moisture in check, night after night.

How the summer side keeps you fresh

The summer side is crafted from linen and silk. Linen disperses heat and allows air to circulate freely, so your skin stays dry. Silk adds lightness and a smooth hand feel while remaining naturally hypoallergenic. The result is a surface that feels fresh to the touch: ideal for warm nights and for sleepers who tend to overheat. Explore how we treat noble fibers in Cashmere Couture￼ (our materials philosophy applies across the range), and pair your bed with a breathable summer layer like Top.

Why the winter side feels naturally warm

When the air turns cooler, the winter side comes into play. We use cashmere and fine wool for their unique ability to insulate without trapping moisture. Wool fibers hold tiny pockets of air that retain warmth while wicking humidity away; cashmere enhances softness and provides a comforting, cocoon-like feel. See our full Mattresses collection￼ to choose the construction and firmness that suit your body.

A healthy microclimate for year-round sleep

Seasonal comfort is about more than warmth or coolness. By pairing breathable fibers on both faces with hand-nested pocket springs, the mattress maintains constant airflow. Excess heat and humidity move out; fresh air moves in. This balanced microclimate supports deeper, more continuous sleep. Looking for a complete setup? Discover our Bed Systems￼ designed to optimise ventilation and support.

Who benefits from a dual-sided mattress

If your bedroom experiences seasonal temperature swings, a two-sided construction is a quiet advantage. Hot sleepers appreciate the linen-and-silk touch in summer. Cold sleepers feel at home on the cashmere-and-wool face in winter. Families with guest rooms gain flexibility without changing bedding. Hospitality spaces benefit from consistent guest comfort across the year. And for anyone seeking a natural mattress with genuine performance, dual-sided design is a smart, sustainable choice.

Care: when and how to switch sides

To keep performance at its best, use the summer side during warmer months and the winter side when temperatures drop. Rotate head-to-foot regularly to even out wear, and flip seasonally to the appropriate face. Because our mattresses are made from natural, resilient fibers over pocket springs, the comfort evolves subtly with you, retaining elasticity and support for years.

Handmade comfort, consciously made

Every Midsummer mattress is built by hand in Italy using natural materials and traditional methods. We avoid synthetic foams and petroleum-based components in favor of breathable fibers that work in harmony with the body. After 15 years, you can return your mattress to our atelier for a complete refresh: fibers are re-carded, the interior is checked, and a new cover is fitted, so your bed begins again with almost no waste. That is luxury designed to last.

Sleep the season you’re in

Summer linen and silk for freshness. Winter wool and cashmere for warmth. A single mattress, two perfected experiences. Start by taking our quick Sleep Assesment below to understand your needs, then explore Mattresses￼ to find your match.

Как летняя сторона помогает оставаться в тонусе

Летняя сторона изготовлена из льна и шелка. Лен рассеивает тепло и обеспечивает свободную циркуляцию воздуха, благодаря чему ваша кожа остается сухой. Когда воздух становится холоднее, в дело вступает зимняя сторона. Мы используем кашемир и тонкую шерсть за их уникальную способность сохранять тепло, не задерживая влагу. Сезонный комфорт – это не только тепло или прохлада. Благодаря сочетанию дышащих волокон с обеих сторон и пружин, расположенных вручную, матрас поддерживает постоянную циркуляцию воздуха. Избыточное тепло и влажность выходят наружу, а свежий воздух поступает внутрь. Этот сбалансированный микроклимат способствует более глубокому и непрерывному сну. Ищете полный комплект? Откройте для себя наши системы кроватей, разработанные для оптимизации вентиляции и поддержки.

Кому выгоден двусторонний матрас?

Если в вашей спальне наблюдаются сезонные перепады температуры, двусторонняя конструкция матраса станет несомненным преимуществом. Тем, кто сильно потеет во сне, понравится прикосновение льна и шелка летом. Тем, кто мерзнет, комфортно будет на матрасе с лицевой стороной из кашемира и шерсти зимой. Семьи с гостевыми комнатами получают дополнительную гибкость, не меняя постельное белье. Гостиничные помещения выигрывают от постоянного комфорта гостей в течение всего года. А для тех, кто ищет натуральный матрас с действительно высокими эксплуатационными характеристиками, двусторонняя конструкция — это разумный и экологичный выбор.

Уход: когда и как переходить на другую сторону

Для поддержания оптимального состояния матраса используйте летнюю сторону в теплое время года, а зимнюю — при понижении температуры. Регулярно переворачивайте матрас изголовьем к изножью, чтобы равномерно распределить износ, и меняйте сторону в зависимости от сезона. Поскольку наши матрасы изготовлены из натуральных, упругих волокон поверх пружинного блока, комфорт плавно меняется вместе с вами, сохраняя эластичность и поддержку на протяжении многих лет.

The Material

Horsehair is a long-standing material in premium mattress-making, valued for natural ventilation, moisture regulation, and lasting resilience. Thanks to its physical structure, it helps keep the bed fresher, drier, and comfortable across the seasons.

  • Best for: hot sleepers, humid climates, people who prefer natural materials
  • Main benefits: airflow, moisture release, durable spring and structure
  • Performance over time: strong resistance to flattening compared to many synthetic fibres

What horsehair is and how it’s processed

Horsehair is a natural fiber obtained from the mane and tail of horses. In quality mattress-making, it is carefully selected, washed, and sterilized, then worked without aggressive chemical treatments.

Origin of the natural fiber

After sourcing, the fiber goes through a preparation process to ensure cleanliness, consistency, and performance. Premium producers focus on strict selection and thorough cleaning so the material remains hygienic and stable inside the mattress.

Physical structure: why horsehair is elastic and breathable

Horsehair performs differently from many other fibres because of its natural structure. In practice, it offers:

  • A hollow fibre that supports airflow and moisture release
  • Natural resilience (springiness) that helps it recover after pressure
  • Stable internal air spaces, which support a fresher sleep environment

Key characteristics of horsehair in a mattress

Horsehair is used as a functional layer because it contributes to both the sleep microclimate and the mattress structure. The main characteristics include:

  • Air circulation within the mattress
    The springy fiber helps keep small air channels open between layers.
  • Moisture management and thermal balance
    It helps the bed feel less stuffy and more stable across seasons.
  • Resistance to compression
    It can help preserve loft and structure with regular use.
  • Volume recovery
    Its natural spring supports bounce-back and a responsive feel.

Why horsehair is so breathable

One of horsehair’s best-known qualities is its ability to promote airflow through the mattress. In practical terms:

  • Air circulates continuously within the layers
  • Moisture is released more quickly, helping the mattress feel fresher
  • The bed stays drier and more thermally balanced across seasons

This is why horsehair is often chosen by people who warm up at night, those in humid environments, or anyone who wants a mattress that stays fresh-feeling over time.

Resilience and support over time

Horsehair can help a mattress maintain its structure longer because it:

  • Resists flattening and recovers its loft
  • Maintains volume and elasticity over the years
  • Contributes to a dynamic, responsive feel that stays supportive without feeling rigid

It is particularly effective when paired with springs, micro-coils, and other natural layers, supporting both comfort and long-term performance.

Comparison: horsehair vs synthetic fibres

Performance always depends on the full mattress construction, but horsehair typically differs from synthetics in these areas:

Feature Horsehair Synthetic fibres
Ventilation Supports continuous airflow through the layers More variable, depends on structure and formulation
Resilience Naturally springy and tends to recover well Can soften or compress sooner, depending on quality
Moisture and heat feel Helps release moisture and stay more balanced May retain heat or moisture in some constructions
Durability Often performs well long-term when well made Varies widely by material quality and density

When to choose a mattress with horsehair

  • People who want high breathability and a fresher sleep surface
  • Hot sleepers or those who experience night sweating
  • Anyone prioritizing natural materials over industrial foams and fibres
  • Those looking for stable comfort over years of use
  • Projects where material performance and craftsmanship matter (homes, yachts, hospitality)

Horsehair in Midsummer mattresses

In Midsummer mattresses, horsehair is used as a functional layer for ventilation and support, combined with fine wools and other natural fibres.

Explore Midsummer mattresses · Discover our natural materials

A conscious material choice

Beyond performance, horsehair reflects a philosophy of responsible craftsmanship. It is natural and durable and, when sourced with care, it fits into a supply chain that considers animal welfare. For those investing in long-term comfort with fewer compromises, it remains one of the most meaningful materials in high-end mattress construction.

Airflow, moisture release, and resilience matter, especially when you look at years of use.

FAQ

Is horsehair good for hot sleepers?

Yes. Its structure supports airflow and helps moisture dissipate, which can help the bed feel fresher.

How does horsehair compare to synthetic fibres?

Horsehair is naturally resilient and often resists long-term flattening better than many industrial fibres.

Where is horsehair used inside a mattress?

It is commonly used as a comfort and support layer, often alongside natural wools and above or between spring systems.

  • Mantiene volume ed elasticità nel corso degli anni
  • Contribuisce a una sensazione dinamica e reattiva che rimane di supporto senza risultare rigida

È particolarmente efficace se abbinato a molle, micro-bobine e altri strati naturali, supportando sia il comfort che le prestazioni a lungo termine.

Confronto: crine di cavallo vs fibre sintetiche

Le prestazioni dipendono sempre dalla struttura completa del materasso, ma il crine di cavallo in genere differisce dai materiali sintetici nei seguenti aspetti:

Caratteristica Crine Fibre sintetiche
Ventilazione Supporta il flusso d'aria continuo attraverso gli strati Più variabile, dipende dalla struttura e dalla formulazione
Resilienza Naturalmente elastico e tende a riprendersi bene Può ammorbidirsi o comprimersi prima, a seconda della qualità
Sensazione di umidità e calore Aiuta a rilasciare l'umidità e a rimanere più equilibrato Può trattenere calore o umidità in alcune costruzioni
Durata Spesso funziona bene a lungo termine quando è ben fatto Varia ampiamente in base alla qualità e alla densità del materiale

Quando scegliere un materasso con crine di cavallo

  • Persone che desiderano un'elevata traspirabilità e una superficie di sonno più fresca
  • Dormire con caldo o sudorazione notturna
  • Chiunque dia priorità ai materiali naturali rispetto alle schiume e alle fibre industriali
  • Chi cerca un comfort stabile nel tempo
  • Progetti in cui le prestazioni dei materiali e la lavorazione artigianale sono importanti (case, yacht, ospitalità)

Crine di cavallo nei materassi Midsummer

Nei materassi Midsummer, il crine di cavallo viene utilizzato come strato funzionale per la ventilazione e il supporto , abbinato a lane pregiate e altre fibre naturali.

Esplora i materassi Midsummer · Scopri i nostri materiali naturali

Una scelta consapevole dei materiali

Oltre alle prestazioni, il crine di cavallo riflette una filosofia di artigianato responsabile. È naturale e durevole e, se acquistato con cura, si inserisce in una filiera che tiene conto del benessere degli animali. Per coloro che investono nel comfort a lungo termine con meno compromessi, rimane uno dei materiali più significativi in costruzione di materassi di alta qualità.

Il flusso d'aria, il rilascio dell'umidità e la resilienza sono importanti, soprattutto se si considerano gli anni di utilizzo.

Domande frequenti

Il crine di cavallo è utile per chi dorme al caldo?

Sì. La sua struttura favorisce il passaggio dell'aria e aiuta a dissipare l'umidità, il che può contribuire a far sì che il letto sia più fresco.

In che modo il crine di cavallo si confronta con le fibre sintetiche?

Il crine di cavallo è naturalmente resistente e spesso resiste meglio all'appiattimento a lungo termine rispetto a molte fibre industriali.

Dove viene utilizzato il crine di cavallo all'interno di un materasso?

Viene comunemente utilizzato come strato di comfort e supporto, spesso insieme a lane naturali e sopra o tra i sistemi a molle.

Art inspired beds by Midsummer Milano—where luxury Italian design meets timeless sleep.

 

Why We Created This Bedroom Art Series

A bed is more than furniture; it’s a cultural object that lives in the intimacy of your home. In “The Art of Rest” we place our designer beds inside re-imagined masterpieces, linking bedroom art to daily wellbeing. Each downloadable image shows how comfort, beauty, and storytelling unite in a single piece of sustainable craftsmanship.

Free high-resolution downloads: Use them as mood-board inspiration, wallpapers, or a gentle reminder that rest itself can be a work of art.

 

Iconic Art Reimagined

Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec · Whispers in Yellow


Two figures rest on a Midsummer mattress, elevating Lautrec’s intimate Paris settings with refined upholstery and artisan details.

 

Frida Kahlo · The Sacred Room


Amid roses and symbolism, our bed becomes part of Kahlo’s inner world—a sanctuary for identity, beauty, and restorative sleep.

 

Felice Casorati · Reading in Silence


Architectural stillness meets soft elegance; the bed serves as a pedestal for focused calm.

 

Henri Rousseau · Where Tigers Sleep


A surreal landscape where even the wild find peace—showing how natural materials bring elemental comfort.

 

William Morris · The Botanical Reverie


A fox naps amid ornate flora, proving luxury can speak nature’s language.

 

Pierre-Auguste Renoir · Impression at Rest


Blooming greens, soft light, and effortless romance surround a bed built for generations.

 

René Magritte · The Weight of Dreams


Dreams feel weightless yet meaningful—mirroring the balanced support of natural fibre mattresses.

 

David Hockney · Lines of Lightness


Vivid geometry meets calming comfort; proof that modern art and heritage craft can coexist.

An elegant end table, the ideal companion for a Midsummer bed. The simple three leg design has a remarkably strong character. The table comes in two heights with different diameters and can be arranged in different ways to best suit the space around the bed.

  • 62 × 60h

Finishings

Элегантный приставной столик – идеальное дополнение к кровати в стиле «Midsummer». Простая конструкция с тремя ножками обладает исключительной прочностью. Столик доступен в двух вариантах высоты и диаметра, его можно расположить по-разному, чтобы наилучшим образом вписать в пространство вокруг кровати.
